question: Do exact first-party Fujifilm separated-light dye-density bases identify independently measured Velvia 100F slide spectra, before any source-to-output or photographic rendering claim?

measured_target.conversion: spectral diffuse transmittance percent to optical density using -log10(percent/100); all consumed values must be strictly positive
measured_target.rights_scope: internal research and audit only; redistribution and commercial training unidentified

split.freshness: algorithm-new but measurement rows were consumed by earlier AQ/P6 experiments; this is not a pristine confirmation population

representation.basis_columns: one nonnegative wavelength-constant base-density column plus exact CB1 yellow/magenta/cyan density curves
representation.coefficient_fit: independent scipy.optimize.nnls fit to each measured target spectrum
representation.wrong-stock-control: per-row lower RMSE of the Velvia 50 and Provia 100F bases
representation.important_boundary: coefficients consume each target spectrum and are an oracle representation diagnostic, never an application-time forward operator

stop_rules: Do not alter wavelengths, bases, coefficient sign, split, controls or gates after the formal report.
Failure closes direct measured-spectrum conformance for these exact first-party dye curves without smoothing, peak alignment, extra basis capacity or threshold rescue.
Pass retains a measured source-basis compatibility result only; it does not authorize source-to-spectrum prediction, photographic rendering, calibration, profile compilation or product mapping.
claim_ceiling: Target-dependent spectral representation compatibility between exact first-party Fujifilm dye-density curves and independently measured Velvia 100F manufactured-target spectra; not a forward film response, independent roll/process, scanner calibration, photographic appearance or product profile.
